axiomatization: Balancer V3 Router, UniswapV2 Router02/pair, ERC20s and the sUSDS ERC4626 are minimal mocks defined in the test file (SymTok, SymSUSDS, SymPair, SymUniRouter, SymV3Router). Exit proceeds, LP minted and ERC4626 shares are free symbolic values, not computed; sqrt and pro-rata maths are not modelled. Router02 is modelled only for an empty pair, where it uses the desired amounts. No OZ, Balancer or UniV2 library behaviour is proven. Pair token order is fixed (sUSDS = token0); the sUSDS = token1 ordering is NOT covered.

proofs.property: P3/P6: operator abort() succeeds; for each of BPT, sUSDS, phUSD and USDS the oldPooler balance rises by exactly the escrow's pre-balance, the escrow ends at 0, newPooler, operator and an unrelated holder are unchanged, totalSupply is unchanged
proofs.domain: all 16 symbolic balances (escrow, oldPooler, newPooler, unrelated holder x 4 tokens) < 2^253 (prevents mint overflow); otherwise unbounded

proofs.property: P5: for any caller != operator, abort(), wrapUsds() and exitAndSeed(mode, [m0,m1], deadline) all fail (checked by success flag), with revert data exactly UniPoolerCutoverEscrow__NotOperator(caller), and escrow USDS/BPT balances are unchanged
proofs.domain: caller: any address != operator; escrow USDS/BPT < 2^253; mode in {0,1}; m0, m1, deadline unbounded

proofs.property: P2/P6/P7c: (liveness) if exit proceeds meet both floors and both seed sides are > 0, the operator's exitAndSeed succeeds; (custody) on success the escrow holds 0 BPT/sUSDS/phUSD, the whole BPT balance is burned, the returned liquidity == LP minted == newPooler's LP balance == pair totalSupply, pair reserves and balances == escrow strays + exit proceeds on each side, the unsynced pair donation goes to newPooler only, operator and exit router keep nothing, and every approval is reset to 0
proofs.domain: BPT in (0, 2^128); exit proceeds and escrow strays each < 2^110; unsynced pair donations < 2^110; LP minted in (0, 2^128); floors > 0; deadline offset in (0, 1 day]; mode PROPORTIONAL or RECOVERY; pair starts with zero reserves; sUSDS = token0. Against the axiomatized mocks only.

proofs.property: P8: operator wrapUsds() succeeds if escrow USDS > 0 and fails if it is 0; on success the whole USDS goes to the sUSDS vault, newPooler's sUSDS rises by exactly the returned shares, escrow and operator hold no sUSDS, and the USDS allowance is reset
proofs.domain: escrow USDS, shares, newPooler sUSDS pre-balance each < 2^253; ERC4626 deposit axiomatized (symbolic shares)
proofs.caveat: No dedicated mutant targets this check (see generalityControl)

supersededRuns.note: First run at the default --loop 2. check_abortExactToOldPooler was [ERROR] 'all paths reverted' because the test's 4-iteration setup loop exceeded the unroll bound. That was a harness defect, not a property result. Rerun at --loop 5 with 0 warnings. The other three PASSed in both runs.

generalityControl.contract: Run22EscrowSymbolicMutant (SymMutantEscrow: A abort pays newPooler; B wrapUsds gate removed; C seed leaves 1 wei phUSD and the phUSD post-check is removed)

results.check_abortExactToOldPooler: FAIL (expected, mutant A), counterexample e.g. escrow balances 2^252 each
results.check_nonOperatorReverts: FAIL (expected, mutant B), counterexample caller=0x0, which=1 (wrapUsds)
results.check_exitAndSeedCustody: FAIL (expected, mutant C), counterexample bptBal=2^127, outS=outP=2^109, m0=1, m1=2^109, liq=2^127
results.check_wrapUsdsExact: PASS (no mutation targets wrap custody; B removes only the gate)

generalityControl.verdict: All three targeted properties produce counterexamples on the mutant, so the PASSes on the real escrow are not vacuous identities. The wrap proof has no mutant control. Its ok-branch is reachable because the liveness assertion forces success when USDS > 0.

notCovered: Real Balancer V3 and UniswapV2 behaviour (axiomatized). The fork suites cover it.
Seed against a pair with non-zero reserves. This is the CODE-001 poisoning DoS: the escrow reverts PairNotEmpty, and the mock router also reverts there, so the path is unmodelled.
Reentrancy through malicious token callbacks (mocks have no hooks)
Multi-call sequences (single call per check; the forge/Medusa invariant campaign covers sequences)
